source: v95 pre-touch aim/foot-speed changes fail 3/3 and often create nonfoot contact. Test the already implemented measured-contact capture controller after the first receiver foot collision.
hypothesis: Activating measured receive-contact buffering for 0.20/0.40/0.60 s in the original six-body world can retain the real ball and permit a later receiver foot shot without reducing body safety.
paired_parent: v88 0.35 m, default receive teacher and capture disabled, same consumed scenes
positive_sample_gate: 3/3 six-G1 safe and clean physical transfers; no ball nonfoot collision from initial pass launch through receiver first touch +0.60 s; no robot-robot contact; at least 2/3 true later receiver foot shots >=0.20 s after first touch with outgoing speed >=2.0 m/s. Only then collect privileged labels; never promote without sealed Fresh teacher-free exam.
interpretation: A positive consumed-scene reachability result is not a generalization or promotion claim. A negative result blocks distillation and prompts full-body coupled-contact teacher redesign.
